messages:
sam.support: FYI we got a customer escalation (ACME) after yesterday's rate-policy tweak. They started seeing 429s from our API around 14:24 UTC. I opened a support ticket and dropped a brief repro, but wanted oncall visibility. grafana: https://grafana.redwood/1d/alerts/abc123 :eyes:

deploy-bot: Policy 'rate-policy-v2' applied to canary (10% traffic) by alex.platform at 2025-08-12T14:12:03Z

alex.platform: thanks — I'm pausing any further rollouts. Can someone post a minimal repro and confirm whether these are 429s from the global token bucket or per-customer quota?

maya.prod: quick glance at metrics: canary nodes show a sharp 5m spike, ~1.2k 429 responses clustered to 14:23-14:28. Errors are 429 JSON with code: RATE_EXCEEDED. No auth failures.

maya.prod: snippet from the rate-policy we pushed:
```json
{"id":"rate-policy-v2","scope":"global","per_min":1200,"burst":2000,"enforcement":"strict"}
```

sam.support: customer provided curl repro (sanitized):
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -H "x-customer-id: acme" \
  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"...","max_tokens":100}'
```
They say it used to work for their normal traffic; began failing right after our canary window.

jon.sre: initial hypothesis: enforcement=\"strict\" removes the smoothing we relied on, causing bursty customers to hit 429s even though aggregate looks fine. Two mitigation paths: reduce enforcement or raise burst temporarily. Recommend rollback for canary to v1 while we investigate.

liam.cs: ACME is on Dedicated but their routing hit canary because we route a fraction of control-plane checks to canary for policy testing — this caused their control calls (quota checks) to fail. We need to confirm impact surface for dedicated customers.

alex.platform: noted. I can flip the canary back. What's the safe rollback command?

jon.sre: runbook step (canary rollback):
```bash
# revert policy in config service
rctl policy apply --id rate-policy-v1 --scope canary --force
# purge cached policy on canary nodes (graceful):
rctl nodes refresh --selector canary --wait
```
If we can't do graceful, run `rctl policy disable --id rate-policy-v2 --scope canary` then `nodes refresh`

maya.prod: also recommend we enable header X-RateLimit-Reset in responses for affected traffic so customers can backoff gracefully while we roll.

alex.platform: initiating rollback now, will post status. Holding PR that would promote v2.

deploy-bot: Rollback job started by alex.platform at 2025-08-12T14:33:10Z (job id rb-4421)

sam.support: contacting ACME with ETA ~15m and asking for logs and exact timestamps (they already sent some). I'm opening a ticket linking this thread.

liam.cs: pls confirm whether ACME needs a config change on their side or if this is entirely server side.

maya.prod: server-side only. The enforcement mode exposed burstiness. We'll follow up with a doc showing safe limits for Dedicated customers.

jon.sre: rollback completed at 2025-08-12T14:39:55Z — canary policy back to v1 according to config service. Monitoring now for 10m.

deploy-bot: Rollback completed (rb-4421) by alex.platform at 2025-08-12T14:39:55Z

alex.platform: PR paused (did not promote). I'll prepare a staging test with higher smoothing, smaller slopes, and a canary with synthetic burst traffic before any re-rollout.

sam.support: ACME updated: errors stopped after ~14:42. They asked for a short postmortem and whether we will change headers so their client can backoff. Adding them to the ticket thread.

maya.prod: action items: 1) add X-RateLimit headers on canary responses within 24h 2) create a synthetic burst test that simulates Dedicated control-plane calls 3) review default enforcement setting (strict -> relaxed) for first-stage canaries.

jon.sre: I'll draft the rollback/postmortem notes and tag infra for a small rehearse of the rollback steps next week.

liam.cs: thanks everyone — I’ll drive the customer comms and keep this thread updated. :thumbsup:
